Apply empirical calibration to study estimates

Source: R/Calibration.R
calibrateEstimates.Rd

Fits a systematic-error null distribution from a set of negative-control estimates and uses it to calibrate p-values and confidence intervals for one or more study estimates.

Usage

calibrateEstimates(estimates, negativeControlOutcomes)

Arguments

estimates

A data frame with at least columns `logRr` and `seLogRr`. Any additional columns are passed through unchanged.

negativeControlOutcomes

A data frame with columns `logRr` and `seLogRr` for outcomes known to have no true association with the exposure (true log hazard ratio = 0). At least 2 complete rows are required.

Value

`estimates` with five additional columns:

`calibratedLogRr`

Bias-corrected point estimate on the log scale.

`calibratedSeLogRr`

Standard error of the calibrated log estimate.

`calibratedP`

Two-sided empirically calibrated p-value.

`calibratedCi95Lb`

Lower bound of the calibrated 95% CI (ratio scale).

`calibratedCi95Ub`

Upper bound of the calibrated 95% CI (ratio scale).

Details

The null distribution is fitted with [EmpiricalCalibration::fitNull()] (maximum-likelihood normal on the logRr scale). The fitted null is then converted to a `systematicErrorModel` with [EmpiricalCalibration::convertNullToErrorModel()] before being passed to [EmpiricalCalibration::calibrateConfidenceInterval()], which shifts and inflates the estimate and its confidence interval to account for estimated systematic error. Calibrated p-values come from [EmpiricalCalibration::calibrateP()] (two-sided by default).

Rows in `estimates` with non-finite `logRr` or `seLogRr` receive `NA` for all calibrated columns. Negative controls with non-finite values are silently dropped before fitting the null.

References

Schuemie MJ, Ryan PB, DuMouchel W, Suchard MA, Madigan D. Interpreting observational studies: why empirical calibration is needed to correct p-values. *Stat Med* 2014;33(2):209-218. doi:10.1002/sim.5925

Schuemie MJ, Hripcsak G, Ryan PB, Madigan D, Suchard MA. Robust empirical calibration of p-values using observational data. *Stat Med* 2016;35(22):3833-3844. doi:10.1002/sim.6977

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
negControls <- data.frame(
  logRr   = rnorm(100, mean = 0.05, sd = 0.15),
  seLogRr = rep(0.12, 100)
)
estimates <- data.frame(
  logRr   = c(0.35, -0.10),
  seLogRr = c(0.12, 0.12)
)
calibrated <- calibrateEstimates(estimates, negControls)
} # }
